content_metadata.title: Congressman Keith Ellison on Hillary vs. Bernie

trimmingSuggestions.description: Segments focusing on Hillary Clinton's patriotism could be shortened to prioritize the core discussion about progressive political strategy.

text_to_speech: What is a progressive caucus? It's the people who believe that we should prioritize diplomacy over war, that the average working American should have dignity, respect and fair compensation and should have the right to organize in a labor union that can bargain freely. We believe that every American should retire in dignity and we shouldn't have our senior citizens living in poverty. We're the ones who believe that it's a good thing to make sure that whether you're black, or you're gay, or whatever religion that you might be or you're female -- that these things are not going to limit your life chances, so we're going to be fighting against discrimination of any kind. So everything you just described, all those principles and policies sound an awful lot more like the Bernie Sanders platform than the Hillary Clinton platform, at least. You talk about trade, she has changed her position. She came around and I'm glad about that. How many of you endorsed Sanders? Two of us. So far. So talk to me about that. Well, Hillary Clinton has been a national figure since the early nineties. And I will be among the first to say that she's a person who loves her country and has fought to be a public servant and has maintained her dignity under some very unfair and unrelenting attacks. I do believe that she's not the progressive Bernie Sanders is, but I will say, that you know, in her favor that you can be a progressive and support her, certainly you can. And maybe we need someone that side to pull her over. But I guess the point I'm really interested in is how to do we move the needle if the likes of you and your cohort of 71 feel they have to go with the establishment candidate? I mean at least in the endorsement state, it doesn't mean you're not going to vote for person who wins the nomination at the end, of course. Sure sure, well I guess the point I was building to, maybe too slowly, is that she locked a lot of people in before Bernie ever got in. And then those same people are reluctant to just abandon her after Bernie really got in and started showing well. So that's what I really think -- I think we probably have at least 10, 12 more people if they would have started out the same time running for president.
